Acetylene bonding
Start with the σ framework
Panel (a) separates the orbital pieces. The orange sp hybrid lobes overlap end-to-end to make three σ bonds: two C-H σ bonds and one C-C σ bond.
Click any σ or π lobe to identify its overlap mode and bond-order contribution.

plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), that together depict the complete bonding framework in acetylene (C2H2), distinguishing the sigma bonds formed by sp hybrid orbitals from the two pi bonds formed by unhybridized p orbitals. Panel (a) shows the individual orbital interactions: three σ bonds are labeled — two C–H σ bonds at the outer ends of the molecule and one C–C σ bond in the center, all formed by the end-on overlap of sp hybrid orbital lobes (orange) meeting at the two carbon atom centers (black dots) — while four unhybridized p orbitals (rendered as red and blue lobes extending above, below, and to the sides of the C–C axis) overlap side by side in two perpendicular planes, with dashed lines connecting opposite lobes to indicate the lateral overlap regions that constitute the two π bonds. Panel (b) shows the overall spatial appearance of the bonding: the orange σ-bond lobes form a linear framework through the molecule, while one π bond (red lobes) wraps above and below the C–C axis and a second π bond (blue lobes) extends in front of and behind the axis, each labeled "One π bond" and "Second π bond" respectively, together encircling the C–C σ bond. This figure establishes the C≡C triple bond in acetylene as the combination of one σ bond and two mutually perpendicular π bonds, and demonstrates how sp hybridization leaves two unhybridized p orbitals per carbon available for the side-on overlaps that enforce the linear molecular geometry.

interactions.teaches: The acetylene triple bond is built in layers: first the linear sigma framework, then two mutually perpendicular pi overlaps added around the C-C axis
Selecting a lobe distinguishes end-to-end sigma overlap from side-to-side pi overlap and shows that the C-C triple bond has one sigma contribution plus two pi contributions

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a horizontal molecular axis along world X. Approximate scale: total visible molecule width about 8 units, height about 3.4 units, depth about 2.4 units. Place carbon nuclei at x=-1.15 and x=1.15, y=0, z=0 as small black spheres radius 0.055. Place hydrogen 1s orbitals at x=-3.65 and x=3.65 as blue spheres radius 0.32, color #7ea2d8 with darker rim #456da8. Orange sigma lobes color #f8b334 to #ffd66a, semi-gloss, slightly transparent where overlapping. Left C-H sigma lobe is an elongated ellipsoid centered near x=-2.55, oriented along X, length about 1.75, radius about 0.38, tapered visually toward the carbon dot. C-C sigma is two overlapping orange ellipsoids centered near x=-0.55 and x=0.55, each length about 1.25 along X and radius about 0.36, meeting in the middle. Right C-H sigma lobe mirrors the left at x=2.55. In panel (a), show localized p orbitals on each carbon: red vertical p orbitals lie in the XY plane with upper and lower ellipsoid lobes centered around y=+0.85 and y=-0.85 at x=-1.15 and x=1.15, color #ef6a75; blue p orbitals lie in the XZ/depth plane with visible lobes offset diagonally/down-right in the source, color #79a7df, centered around z=+0.65 and z=-0.65 with slight y offsets so they read behind/in front. Dashed overlap guide lines are dark gray #666666, horizontal, connecting left and right corresponding p lobes at approximately y=+1.25, +0.55, -0.55, and -1.25. Put small dark phase minus signs in each p lobe as in the source. In panel (b), replace separated p lobes with continuous pi clouds: red pi cloud is two long rounded lobes spanning x=-1.65 to x=1.65 above and below the C-C axis, centered y=+0.75 and y=-0.75, flattened through depth, color #ef6a75 at opacity about 0.72. Blue pi cloud is perpendicular to the red cloud and should wrap in front/behind the C-C axis, visible as a broad lower/front lobe and side/back lobe, color #6f9ed7 at opacity about 0.65. The C-C bond order contributions for the click callout are: central C-C σ bond = 1, red π bond = 1, blue π bond = 1, total C-C bond order = 3. C-H σ bonds each contribute one σ bond to the corresponding C-H single bond, not to the C-C bond order. Labels should match the source: black sans-serif text, large 'σ bond' labels above the three sigma bonds in panel (a), 'One π bond' above-left/center in panel (b), and 'Second π bond' at upper right in panel (b).
interactionPlan.notes: Model orbitals as smooth ellipsoids or metaball-like blended meshes with soft Phong/standard material highlights to resemble textbook orbital blobs. Use transparent materials with depth sorting carefully controlled so the orange sigma framework remains visible through the pi clouds in panel (b). The bondView toggle should not display both panels side by side; it should replace the visible geometry and labels in one centered scene. Use raycasting on grouped bond components for selectBondLobe: left C-H sigma, C-C sigma, right C-H sigma, red pi bond, and blue pi bond. On click, brighten the selected group, add a thin dark outline or halo, and show a compact callout near the selected lobe. Keep the default camera close to the source front view, but allow orbiting to reveal the perpendicularity of the red and blue pi systems.

authoredContext:
In molecules with sp hybrid orbitals, two unhybridized p orbitals remain on the atom ( ). We find this situation in acetylene, H−C≡C−H , which is a linear molecule. The sp hybrid orbitals of the two carbon atoms overlap end to end to form a σ bond between the carbon atoms ( ). The remaining sp orbitals form σ bonds with hydrogen atoms. The two unhybridized p orbitals per carbon are positioned such that they overlap side by side and, hence, form two π bonds. The two carbon atoms of acetylene are thus bound together by one σ bond and two π bonds, giving a triple bond.

(a) In the acetylene molecule, C 2 H 2, there are two C–H σ bonds and a C ≡ C triple bond involving one C–C σ bond and two C–C π bonds. The dashed lines, each connecting two lobes, indicate the side-by-side overlap of the four unhybridized p orbitals. (b) This shows the overall outline of the bonds in C 2 H 2 . The two lobes of each of the π bonds are positioned across from each other around the line of the C–C σ bond.

Two diagrams are shown and labeled, “a” and “b.” Diagram a shows two carbon atoms with two purple balloon-like orbitals arranged in a plane around each of them, and four red balloon-like orbitals arranged along the y and z axes perpendicular to the plane of the molecule. There is an overlap of two of the purple orbitals in between the two carbon atoms. The other two purple orbitals that face the outside of the molecule are shown interacting with spherical blue orbitals from two hydrogen atoms. Diagram b depicts a similar image to diagram a, but the red, vertical orbitals are interacting above and below and to the front and back of the plane of the molecule to form two areas labeled, “One pi bond,” and, “Second pi bond,” each respectively.

Hybridization involves only σ bonds, lone pairs of electrons, and single unpaired electrons (radicals). Structures that account for these features describe the correct hybridization of the atoms. However, many structures also include resonance forms. Remember that resonance forms occur when various arrangements of π bonds are possible. Since the arrangement of π bonds involves only the unhybridized orbitals, resonance does not influence the assignment of hybridization.

discrepancies: The default panel (a) is shown at a strong diagonal 3D angle, whereas the source panel (a) is a mostly front-facing horizontal molecular diagram.
The original shows panels (a) and (b) side by side simultaneously; the generated version hides one behind a dropdown/button toggle, reducing the source's comparative layout.
An extra selected-bond callout box appears over the central orbitals and is not present in the source figure.
Panel (a) orbital placement is more spatially cluttered than the source: the blue/red p orbitals and central σ overlap are less cleanly separated.
The generated annotations omit the exact two-leader structure for the π-bond labels in the default view because panel (b) is not initially visible.
evaluation.notes: The molecular-orbital primitives and labels are mostly correct and the interactions are useful, but the default camera/composition and extra callout make it less faithful to the textbook figure.
action_items: Set the initial view closer to the source: horizontal molecule axis with a front-facing orthographic view for panel (a).
Reduce or hide the selected-bond callout by default so it does not cover the central orbitals.
Improve panel (a) spacing so red and blue p orbitals are visually separated like the source rather than clustered around the center.
Consider a split-screen option showing panels (a) and (b) side by side to match the original composition.

feedback.rationale: The concept and primitives are correct, but the main issues are implementation-level camera, layout, spacing, and extra callout artifacts that the generator can fix.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), that together depict the complete bonding framework in acetylene (C2H2), distinguishing the sigma bonds formed by sp hybrid orbitals from the two pi bonds formed by unhybridized p orbitals. Panel (a) shows the individual orbital interactions: three σ bonds are labeled — two C–H σ bonds at the outer ends of the molecule and one C–C σ bond in the center, all formed by the end-on overlap of sp hybrid orbital lobes (orange) meeting at the two carbon atom centers (black dots) — while four unhybridized p orbitals (rendered as red and blue lobes extending above, below, and to the sides of the C–C axis) overlap side by side in two perpendicular planes, with dashed lines connecting opposite lobes to indicate the lateral overlap regions that constitute the two π bonds. Panel (b) shows the overall spatial appearance of the bonding: the orange σ-bond lobes form a linear framework through the molecule, while one π bond (red lobes) wraps above and below the C–C axis and a second π bond (blue lobes) extends in front of and behind the axis, each labeled "One π bond" and "Second π bond" respectively, together encircling the C–C σ bond. This figure establishes the C≡C triple bond in acetylene as the combination of one σ bond and two mutually perpendicular π bonds, and demonstrates how sp hybridization leaves two unhybridized p orbitals per carbon available for the side-on overlaps that enforce the linear molecular geometry.
